text:
maria_k: Heads up — found a proxy header leak that can be used to route requests across workspaces. Not good.
kevinw: Details? how is it observed?
maria_k: Saw requests with X-Forwarded-Workspace: <workspace-id> being honored by internal service auth layer. Repro steps below.
ops_jen: Oof. Any production impact yet?
maria_k: Limited. Customer A's request with forged header hit Customer B's admin-only endpoint and returned 403->200 when header was accepted.
security-paul: Can you paste the request/response? redact ids pls.
maria_k: ```
POST /v1/admin/keys HTTP/1.1
Host: internal-api.redwood.local
X-Forwarded-Workspace: wksp-12345
Authorization: Bearer <token-for-wksp-99999>
```
kevinw: So proxy is forwarding the header and auth layer trusts it instead of validating token workspace claim?
sara_reed: That matches: token validation code checks Authorization then falls back to header caste if token tenant mismatch. Legacy fast-path for internal calls.
ops_jen: Who owns the proxy config? Is it nginx/middlebox?
kevinw: Edge proxy team controls it, but internal LB also strips/forwards headers based on allowlist. Looks like a recent change in lb-rules allowed X-Forwarded-Workspace through for health checks.
security-paul: Immediate mitigation: add a rule to drop X-Forwarded-Workspace in the internal LB for public-facing paths. Can ops do a hotfix?
ops_jen: I can push a drop-header rule to staging now and then prod in 10m if tests pass.
maria_k: Also need a quick patch to auth service to prefer token claims over header and log mismatches to audit.
kevinw: I'll open a PR to reject requests where token workspace != header and header present. Returns 401 instead of falling back.
sara_reed: Audit note: our logs show missing audit entries when fallback happened. audit-bot, can you check if those requests generated any workspace-level audit events?
audit-bot: checking logs for workspace ID patterns... found 7 requests in last 3h where auth fallback allowed header override; no workspace_audit events recorded for those.
security-paul: That means we lost visibility. Need to surface those as incidents and notify affected customers. Also check KMS access — could a vault unwrap have been attempted?
kevinw: KMS bindings: they are scoped by workspace in policy; but the API call we saw was admin/keys, which can touch KMS. We'll verify if any decrypt/unwrap calls occurred under the wrong principal.
ops_jen: Rolling header-drop to prod now. ETA 8m.
maria_k: Testing repro against staging after drop. If header is stripped, the endpoint returns 403 as expected.
security-paul: Action items: 1) ops: drop header at LB (in flight) 2) eng-auth (kevin): PR to reject token/header mismatch + log 3) eng-audit (sara): backfill audit events and surface to CS 4) security: prepare customer notif template.
kevinw: PR: https://github.com/redwood/eng-auth/pull/482 — adds strict header-check + unit tests.
sara_reed: I'll run a log search and create a timeline in the incident ticket. Ticket: INC-2026-1987 (internal).
ops_jen: Prod change complete. Verified header is stripped at LB for public ingress.
maria_k: Confirmed staging repro fails now (good).
audit-bot: backfill job started for the 7 suspicious requests. estimated 5m.
security-paul: We should also audit KMS logs (HSM) for any cross-workspace decrypts — assign to kevin.
kevinw: On it. Running kms access logs query now.
sara_reed: CS: I'm drafting a short note for impacted customers saying we detected potential header misuse but no evidence of secret material exfiltration; will sync with legal.
security-paul: Good. After patch merged, schedule a postmortem and a follow-up to remove legacy header-trust fast-path entirely.
maria_k: Postmortem owner? I can take it with kevin and sara.
kevinw: LGTM. I'll shepherd the PR and KMS log checks.
ops_jen: Leaving more granular LB rules to infra team for a longer term fix.
security-paul: Closing loop: once audit backfill and KMS check are done, we update the ticket and notify stakeholders. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
maria_k: Thanks team. I'll upload repro logs to INC-2026-1987 and add mitigation notes.
kevinw: KMS logs show no decrypts for wrong workspace — no evidence of key use. Will attach query results to ticket.
sara_reed: Postmortem doc created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-1987/postmortem (draft).
security-paul: Keep incident severity at P2 for now until legal signs off on customer communication.
maria_k: ack.
kevinw: PR merged, deploy scheduled in next deploy window.
ops_jen: Final check: LB rule will remain enforced. Reopen if anything weird shows up.
security-paul: Thanks. End of thread.
